name: Budd, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the judiciary should not order increased compensation rates for bar advocates because CPCS failed to show extraordinary circumstances, and doing so would violate the separation of powers by interfering with the Legislature's authority over appropriations.

name: DEWAR, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Commonwealth failed to meet its burden to show that the twenty-four hour delay in stopping the defendant for a civil traffic infraction was reasonable, thereby violating art. 14 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights.

name: Wolohojian, J.
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion, arguing that legislative immunity does not cover non-legislative campaign activities and that the grand juror's exclusion did not prejudice the defendant.

name: Kafker, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the pension forfeiture was not an excessive fine or cruel and unusual punishment under Article 26 of the Massachusetts Constitution.

name: Kafker
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion that the department failed to demonstrate that exempting the child from vaccinations would substantially hinder the fulfillment of the department's interests in promoting child health, thus violating the parents' free exercise rights.

name: GAZIANO, J.
description: Concurred, delivering the opinion of the court that the initial GPS monitoring was a reasonable search and the subsequent data retrieval was not a search under art. 14.

name: Gaziano, J.
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion affirming the dismissal of indictments due to the Commonwealth's deliberate non-compliance with discovery orders for an equal protection claim.

name: GAZIANO, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the constitutionally mandated exception to the indigency statute applies to allow funds for expert services to safeguard a disabled prisoner's constitutional right to a parole hearing free of discrimination on the basis of disability.

name: Wendlandt, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the decision to apply Brown only prospectively was neutral, did not have a discriminatory purpose, did not burden a fundamental right, and passed rational basis review, thus not violating equal protection principles.

name: Wendlandt, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the bylaw is not preempted by the Tobacco Act as it is not inconsistent, contrary, or conflicting with the state's minimum age standard, and that it is rationally related to a legitimate government interest without violating equal protection.

name: Lowy, J.
description: Concurred, argued that not every adverse credibility finding means an officer lied, and emphasized the distinction between the duty of investigation and the duty of inquiry.

name: Cypher, J.
description: Concurred with Justice Lowy's separate opinion.

name: Budd, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that youth matters in determining constitutional punishment and mandatory life without parole for emerging adults violates Article 26.

name: Kafker, J.
description: Concurred, argued that scientific evidence and legislative recognition for 18-20 year olds, similar to juveniles in Diatchenko I, requires extending constitutional protections against life without parole.

name: Wendlandt, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court has a constitutional duty to ensure punishments are proportionate, and scientific data and societal recognition show young adults (18-20) share characteristics with juveniles, making life without parole unconstitutional for them.

name: Lowy, J.
description: Dissented, argued that defining punishment is an exclusive legislative function and mandatory life without parole for adults (18+) for first-degree murder does not violate Article 26.

name: Cypher, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the court is overstepping the Legislature's role in defining punishment and that science alone should not dictate legal lines for adulthood, especially when the Legislature has already defined 18 as the age of majority.

name: GAZIANO, J.
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion affirming the denial of the motion to suppress, finding reasonable suspicion and a race-neutral reason for the stop.

name: CYPHER, J.
description: Concurred in part, but dissented from the court's decision to limit the collective knowledge doctrine, arguing it should be applied as historically understood.

name: WENDLANDT, J.
description: Concurred with the finding of reasonable suspicion but dissented from the court's decision to limit the collective knowledge doctrine, arguing it should be rejected in all its forms.

name: Kafker, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the town's civility code violates the rights to assembly and free speech under Articles 19 and 16 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights by imposing content-based restrictions on political speech.

name: GAZIANO, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights does not protect a fundamental right to physician-assisted suicide, and the law of manslaughter may prohibit physician-assisted suicide without offending constitutional protections.

name: CYPHER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the proposed right to physician-assisted suicide finds no support in the State Constitution, but did not foreclose the possibility that some applications of criminal statutes might intolerably intrude on patient freedom.

name: WENDLANDT, J.
description: Concurred in the judgment that there is no fundamental right to physician-assisted suicide, but dissented from the dismissal of Kligler's claims, arguing Kligler presented an actual controversy.

name: Budd, C.J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part with Justice Wendlandt's opinion.

name: WENDLANDT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the board's regulations, which do not require common-law fraud elements, are rationally related to protecting public confidence and health, and thus do not offend due process.

name: Budd, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the board's decision was consistent with the juvenile offender's right to a meaningful opportunity for parole, as it considered youth-related factors and concluded the plaintiff was not yet rehabilitated.

name: KAFKER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the VOTES Act is constitutional as the Legislature has broad powers to regulate elections and enhance voting opportunities, and the challenged provisions do not violate the Massachusetts or U.S. Constitutions.

name: Lowy, J.
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion, finding the Attorney General's summary and ballot statements fair and compliant with legal requirements.

name: Kafker, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the initiative petitions contained two substantively distinct policy decisions, violating the related subjects requirement of art. 48, and that the obscure language used could confuse voters.

name: Wendlandt, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Initiative Petition 21-03's various provisions form an integrated scheme of regulation for alcohol sales, presenting a unified statement of public policy that meets Article 48's related subjects requirement.

name: CYPHER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the officers had reasonable suspicion based on the totality of circumstances, including a companion's distracting behavior, prior firearm involvement, gang affiliations, and the high-crime area, to believe the defendant might be armed and dangerous.

name: LOWY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the inference of a diversionary tactic by the companion was reasonable, justifying the patfrisk, while acknowledging concerns about racial disparities.

name: WENDLANDT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the decision correctly applied the reasonable suspicion standard based on the totality of circumstances and does not contribute to systematic racism.

name: BUDD, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the patfrisk was unconstitutional as the officers' suspicion was not objectively reasonable, leading to an erosion of constitutional rights and exacerbating racial disparities.

name: GAZIANO, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the court's ruling relied on subjective and speculative beliefs rather than specific articulable facts, thereby undermining the reasonable suspicion standard and infringing constitutional rights.

name: GEORGES, J.
description: Dissented, joined Justice Gaziano's dissenting opinion.

name: Lowy, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the separate standing requirement under Article 14 should be abolished, requiring only a reasonable expectation of privacy to contest a search or seizure, but found the defendant lacked such an expectation in this case.

name: GAZIANO, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the whistleblower act applies to the dismissal of the SORB chair by the Governor, that the Governor's actions are attributable to the Commonwealth, and that applying the act does not violate separation of powers or conflict with other statutes.

name: GAZIANO, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that Delgado-Rivera had no reasonable expectation of privacy in text messages sent to and stored on another person's cellular telephone, and therefore lacked standing to challenge the search.

name: CYPHER, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that a reasonable expectation of privacy alone is sufficient to establish standing under Article 14, and sought to clarify the court's case law regarding standing and privacy.
